deviations.what: fetch returns None for a 404 (and a search by identifier finds nothing) instead of raising RegistryUnavailable; other non-200 answers, network errors, timeouts and unreadable answers raise it.
deviations.why: A 404 from the record endpoints is the registry saying there is no such record; reading it as unavailable would tell a manager the registry is down when they mistyped an identifier. tasks.md lists a timeout, a connection error and a 500, not a 404.

deviations.what: models.py: the ORCID and ROR patterns became the constants ORCID_PATTERN and ROR_PATTERN, used by Person.clean, Organization.clean and the registries.
deviations.why: The brief asks the registries to reuse the pattern near Person; it was a literal inside a method. Behaviour of the two clean methods is unchanged.

deviations.what: AffiliationChoice.choice() (story 2) selects a person's primary affiliation before it falls back to the suggested employer.
deviations.why: A person the portal already holds under an ORCID iD should be offered their own affiliations, with the primary selected (FR-023); nothing else sets a suggestion.

deviations.what: The country of an organization entered by hand is a name or a code in the unchanged text input, not a select.
deviations.why: A select changes what the approved card draws; the brief allows it only when nothing else changes.

concerns: State of a person entered by hand with an email address: active, not claimed, email stored, unusable password, so account_state is INVITED, can_sign_in() is false, no social account, listed by Person.objects.invited(). Without an email: GHOST. Nothing is sent by the page. But allauth finds users by Person.email whatever their password, and a throwaway test (not kept) showed that posting the stored address to the portal's password reset page mails it, while a password sign-in fails. The brief says the stored email must not make the person able to receive mail; I could not meet that without changing the account adapter or sign-in settings, which this story does not touch. Needs a maintainer decision (decisions D19).

A profile made from ORCID or ROR saves a ContributorIdentifier, whose existing AFTER_CREATE hook queues sync_contributor_identifier after commit. On a portal with a task broker that task calls ORCID or ROR, with its own ten-second timeout, and fills in the profile. The tests run no on_commit callbacks, so none ran.

On the chosen step the employer shown comes from the fetched record (the first current employment), while the search list shows the first institution-name of the search. For a person with several current employers the two can differ (the recorded record lists Wesleyan first, the recorded search lists Brown first).
A search term is passed to ORCID as the q parameter unchanged, so a manager can use its query syntax. It is encoded by requests and can only widen or narrow what the public search returns.
ORCID answers 409 for a locked or deactivated record; fetch reads any non-200 other than 404 as unavailable.
